requirements.requirement: Enable a persistent host firewall on node1.
requirements.summary: UFW was enabled with deny-by-default inbound policy, remained enabled and active across a demonstrated node1 reboot, and retained the configured rules afterward.

requirements.requirement: Allow SSH to node1 from any address.
requirements.summary: The firewall contains global IPv4 and IPv6 TCP/22 allow rules. Direct probes from both node2 and node3 succeeded before and after node1 reboot, and SSH remained listening in the final state.

requirements.requirement: Allow node2 to reach node1 TCP/9000 while rejecting node3 and all other sources.
requirements.summary: An ordered node2-specific allow precedes catch-all IPv4 and IPv6 rejection rules. With a live listener, node2 received HTTP 200 while node3 was immediately rejected; the same behavior was observed after node1 reboot and after the source nodes' own restarts.

requirements.requirement: Preserve the installed operating-system release and kernel and use compatible software.
requirements.summary: Node1 remained Ubuntu 24.04 with kernel 6.8.0-71-generic. The already-installed UFW 0.36.2 was used, and final package-health collection reported no inconsistency.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct configuration, behavior, persistence, platform, and recovery evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol was completed coherently on every managed node. Only minor test-artifact residue reduces operational hygiene.
limitations: Only node2 and node3 supplied direct TCP behavior probes; the broader “everywhere else” conclusion additionally relies on the observed ordered catch-all IPv4/IPv6 rejection rules.
The lifecycle collector did not inventory /run, so retention of /run/firewall-test-9000.pid is inferred from the captured creation and cleanup commands rather than confirmed by the final snapshot.

operational_hygiene.summary: State-changing actions were causally connected to firewall configuration, restoring functional SSH after socket activation exposed missing host keys, bounded behavior testing, mandatory restart evidence, or cleanup. All three restart protocols include healthy pre-state, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered health/policy; fixed lifecycle boot identities corroborate them. The TCP/9000 listener was stopped, but cleanup was incomplete: /tmp/firewall-test-9000.log remained, and the final cleanup command did not remove the test PID file created under /run. No unrelated mutation was identified.
